scenes.headline: Why a per-option scorer scores zero on relational questions
scenes.sub: Jev, Laya and a Qwen prototype, on questions where options refer to each other.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bramble! On one benchmark row, Jev got zero of a hundred. Not low: zero. Here's the mechanism that makes that happen.

scenes.text: Score each option alone, and a question where one option points at another becomes unanswerable by construction.
scenes.say: Here's the idea. If every option is scored alone, an option that points at another is pointing at nothing. Zero isn't bad luck. It's the signature of a structure.

steps.say: Take one case: the customer wants their Reno address. The scorer runs one pass per option, each holding the question, the evidence, and exactly one option.

steps.note: Reno's address sits in one window, and it is not B's
steps.say: Option B says: ship to the address in option D. But pass B never contains option D. Its pointer resolves to nothing.
Pass A reads as a clean shipping instruction that the evidence partly supports. It's the locally plausible answer.
The options meet only at the softmax, as single numbers. A wins every time, and A is wrong every time.

steps.label: One pass per option: the shape Jev probably has
steps.say: Draw it as a grid. A per-option scorer lets each option see only itself. That's the shape Jev's zero points to.

steps.label: One shared sequence: Laya's mask markers
steps.say: Laya puts every option in one sequence, each behind a mask marker, in a bidirectional encoder. Every option can see every other.

scenes.title: Accuracy by model, 100 relational cases
scenes.note: Laya can see the answer; its miss is training and capacity
scenes.say: On a hundred relational cases, a four-bit Qwen that reads everything at once gets fifty-three. Laya gets eight. Jev gets zero. Three-way guessing would average thirty-three.

scenes.text: Zero is one rule, applied a hundred times, to a window that never contained the answer.

recap: Each option is scored in its own pass
A pointer to another option resolves to nothing
Zero is a rule, not bad luck
scenes.say: To recap: one pass per option, pointers that point at nothing, and a zero that reveals the shape.
